source_snapshot.procedure: Offers two different DRAM/MCA BIOS profiles, unlocks HDT, lists valid UMCs, then runs `--dramecc --errormode 1 --address 0x1000 --enablemcapolling 0 --errortype 0` once with no explicit UMC or slot selector.

source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool 1.1 DRAM settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → DRAM Corrected Error Counter Enable: NoLeakMode c. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → DRAM Corrected Error Counter Start Count: FFFE (Deviate from default setting FFF5) d. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → Data Poisoning: Auto e. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → Disable Memory Error Injection: False f. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → ECC Configuration → DRAM UECC Retry: Disabled g. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After SyncFlood: Enabled 1.2 MCA settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → DRAM Corrected Error Counter Enable: Disabled c. CPU Common Options → MCA Error Thresh Enable: True d. UMC Common Options → MCA Error Thresh Count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5) d. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → Data Poisoning: Auto e. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → Disable Memory Error Injection: False f. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → ECC Configuration → DRAM UECC Retry: Disabled g. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After SyncFlood: Enabled 2. Unlock CPU via HDT. 3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022. 4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software. 5. Enter the following commands: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --listvalidumc 6. Explicit Address based correctable error injection, enter command: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --dramecc --errormode 1 --address 0x1000 --enablemcapolling 0 --errortype 0 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed. 4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- DRAM Correctable Explicit Address Based ECC error (AMD RAS): inject via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool after HDT/unlock + BIOS DDR RAS knobs, then verify with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -180 | grep -iE 'corrected|address.error|ecc'; echo __DRAM_Correctable_Explicit_Address_Based_ECC_error; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1". Agent stages/verifies the injection evidence; the tool inject step itself is interactive/HW-level.

disposition_reason: Explicit-address injection differs from topology-directed injection because correctness depends on what address space the tool consumes and whether that page remains mapped to the intended DIMM. Interleave and hashing can distribute nearby addresses across channels, so a numeric address is not a slot identity. A low 0x1000 value may be an offset, a system address or invalid depending on tool revision; only package documentation and a live map can decide. Corrected-event evidence must carry the same address/location chain, not merely match the word ECC. test_case.test_name: Memory slot 1~N — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Validate the AMD tool's explicit-address correctable DRAM path for each required populated slot, proving that errormode 1 targets the intended physical DIMM and produces a corrected event without degrading memory service.
required_package: Owned reserved physical page per target and proof whether literal 0x1000 is valid
Decision whether DRAM 1.1 and MCA 1.2 are alternatives, separate checkpoints or cumulative
AMD tool/spec version/hash/license and `dramecc`, errormode 1, mcapolling 0 and errortype 0 semantics
Per-address/slot corrected MCA/EDAC/APEI/WHEA/rasdaemon/BMC oracle and timeout
BIOS threshold deviation, abort, recovery, page cleanup and restoration plan
test_case.test_command: Select one approved DRAM or MCA BIOS profile; inventory UMC/channel/DIMM/rank/slot topology; reserve an OS-owned test page and translate its system physical address through interleave/hash rules; confirm `--dramecc --errormode 1` consumes that address directly; perform one CE for each approved slot; correlate exact address, syndrome/location and corrected counters across tool, MCA/EDAC/APEI or WHEA and management evidence; release the page and restore BIOS/HDT/injection state.
test_case.expected_result: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed. 4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.

safety_gate: Use a dedicated ECC SUT with independent console and recoverable workload
Never inject literal 0x1000 unless current firmware/OS memory maps prove it is an owned backed page
Pin or reserve each target page so allocation/migration cannot change during the injection
Apply only the approved BIOS profile; stop on wrong slot, UCE escalation, storm, reset, poison persistence or memory degradation
No automatic retry; release test allocation and restore/diff injection, HDT and BIOS state
expected_evidence: Per-target page reservation plus address-to-slot translation proof
Full errormode-1 CE transcript and exact corrected address/location/syndrome evidence within timeout
Page release, injector disablement, BIOS/HDT restoration and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: If this tool revision interprets 0x1000 as an offset relative to a separately selected UMC rather than a system physical address, engineering must provide that selector and translation contract before execution.

source_conflict.reason: The source claims Memory slot 1~N but executes one explicit address 0x1000 without UMC selection or address-to-slot proof after `--listvalidumc`. The DRAM and MCA profiles conflict on counter enable and are not scoped; timeout is undefined, and Windows is offered while Criteria requires dmesg.
